title: Why Does a Spoon Look Broken in Water?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why does a spoon look broken in water?
Pull it out, and it's perfectly straight.
You see the spoon by the light that leaves it and reaches your eye.
In water, light travels about a quarter slower than in air.
So a ray leaving the water at a slant bends at the surface, tipping flatter.
But your brain assumes the ray never bent.
It traces each ray straight back, to a spot higher than the spoon really is.
The part in the air appears where it is. The part under water appears lifted.
So the spoon seems to snap right at the surface.
The spoon isn't bent. The light is.
